analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The head changed range is lines 320-323, where documentation rows for new Nemotron Super MTP environment variables were added: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP, _DEPTH and _VERIFICATION. They point to NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift (Setting.resolve). The patch excerpt is truncated after the third row's description and the head text I received starts at line 1 but ends at 311, so I did not see the head text of the changed lines 320-323. I reviewed only the patch excerpt for those lines. The PR does not change any code or security control in the supplied material.

The documented behavior is an opt-in (exact `1`, default off) greedy text speculation with a fixed draft depth of 1 to 3, and rectangular or serial verification. It says the speculating owner refuses media, DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP still disables it, and none of it is forwarded to LaunchAgents. Those statements limit exposure to foreground/local processes by default. They touch TB-007 (the inference engine) and are only loosely related to T-041 (prefix cache). The documented text makes no claim about the prefix cache, encryption, attestation or authorization, so I found no assertion that contradicts the threat model. I could not check the Swift implementation or the unseen portion of the third row. The next pass should verify that the docs match the code (media refusal, the MTP kill switch, no LaunchAgent passthrough) if the source is available. The base text I received covers lines 312-576 and has no overlap with the changed lines, which matches an insert at line 320.
